correctness.rationale: For every integer m≥4 and N=2m+1, α=π/N, positivity at j=m,m−1 gives two inequalities with b coefficient signs s sin(α/2) and −s sin(3α/2), s=(−1)^m. Multiplying by positive complementary sine factors eliminates b and bounds a≤cos(α/2)/[cosα cos(3α/2)]. At equality b=s·2sinα/cos(3α/2) is forced. Set j=m−r, x_r=(2r+1)α/2∈(0,π/2], and y=sin x_r. Feasibility values split as q_+(y)=2Ay²+By+1−A (even r) and q_−(y)=2Ay²−By+1−A (odd r). The plus quadratic is increasing for y≥0 and vanishes at first even sample; the minus quadratic has roots of opposite sign and vanishes at first odd sample. Thus ALL sampled inequalities hold; finite tests are not the infinite proof. Independent floating-point tests passed m=4..200 (197 whole grids), two contacts and dual bound. Source RESULT has literal BEL control characters in place of LaTeX \alpha; semantic mathematics is recoverable, but the public text is malformed.
residual_risks: Requires exactly real even 2-frequency support {1,m} on odd grid, not arbitrary N,k or continuous positivity. Public RESULT.md contains U+0007 BEL before occurrences of lpha, a source-rendering/privacy deliverability blocker.

The new theorem closes the full infinite diagonal with exact sharp value, unique coefficient, two-sample extremal certificate, and explicit N^(−2) sampling gain. This is a natural finite-group harmonic-analysis invariant rather than an arbitrary finite slice or a known-table recomputation.
